title: Capstone verification and explanation
summary: Diagnose and repair a deliberately imperfect field-report project against clean supplied data, separate normal evidence from errors, verify a repeat run, and explain why the evidence supports the result.

content.objective: Inspect a fresh isolated field-report fixture, explain defects in inherited documentation, paths, pipelines, redirection, error handling, and permissions, then repair and directly run an executable bounded Bash script that replaces exact reports from immutable clean data, separates diagnostics, preserves first-run evidence, proves summary repeatability with an empty diff, and documents the verification claims in a concise README and verification note.
content.instructions: Work only in workspace/verification-lab and complete the five tasks in order. This activity is isolated from Lesson 19, so clean-data/system and the deliberately imperfect field-report project are supplied here. Treat every path under clean-data as immutable. Inspect before editing: the inherited README names the wrong run location, report.sh is nonexecutable and contains a wrong relative source path, unquoted expansions, unstable or overbroad pipelines, cumulative summary redirection, and merged diagnostics; the inherited summary is stale false evidence. Repair README.md and report.sh from the stated acceptance criteria, not by patching generated reports. The script must run from field-report as ./report.sh, read only ../clean-data/system, quote path expansions, use bounded find and grep operations, order categories with cut | sort | uniq, replace stale outputs, keep diagnostics only in reports/run-errors.txt, and leave normal completion text in reports/run-output.txt. Add only user execute permission. After a first clean run, save reports/summary.txt as verification/summary-first.txt; run the unchanged script again and redirect diff -u of the saved and current summaries to verification/repeatability.diff. Finish VERIFICATION.md with evidence-backed explanations of source scope, report counts, error separation, repeatability, pipelines, and mode 0744. Do not hand-edit generated reports, modify clean data, use real system paths, sudo, removal commands, broad permissions, recursive grep, find actions, downloads, network access, eval, or writes outside field-report.

Then run cat VERIFICATION.md reports/summary.txt reports/run-output.txt reports/run-errors.txt verification/repeatability.diff. Defend every claim in your own words and identify the file that supports it.

# Field Report

Run from this directory:
./report.sh

The script reads immutable data from ../clean-data/system and replaces six evidence files in reports/.
Normal report data stays in its named files; command diagnostics are kept separately in reports/run-errors.txt.

#!/bin/bash
# Rebuild deterministic evidence from the supplied clean fixture.
source_dir='../clean-data/system'
report_dir='reports'
mkdir -p "$report_dir"
: > "$report_dir/run-errors.txt"
{
  find "$source_dir" -type f -name '*.conf' | sort > "$report_dir/config-files.txt"
  grep -n '^ERROR' "$source_dir/var/log/operations.log" > "$report_dir/errors.txt"
  cut -d ',' -f 2 "$source_dir/var/lib/inventory/assets.csv" | sort | uniq > "$report_dir/categories.txt"
  printf 'Field Report\n' > "$report_dir/summary.txt"
  printf 'Source files: ' >> "$report_dir/summary.txt"
  find "$source_dir" -type f | wc -l >> "$report_dir/summary.txt"
  printf 'Config files: ' >> "$report_dir/summary.txt"
  find "$source_dir" -type f -name '*.conf' | wc -l >> "$report_dir/summary.txt"
  printf 'Error entries: ' >> "$report_dir/summary.txt"
  grep '^ERROR' "$source_dir/var/log/operations.log" | wc -l >> "$report_dir/summary.txt"
  printf 'Field report complete\n' > "$report_dir/run-output.txt"
} 2>> "$report_dir/run-errors.txt"

hints.text: Do not fix what you have not observed. Separate location, source text, generated text, and permission metadata; for each suspicious output, ask which inherited line could produce it.
Use one orientation command, one listing command, and one read-only command over the README, script, and stale summary. Explain the evidence before naming a correction.

From verification-lab, confirm location and names, then use cat with the three paths in the task's stated order. Compare the run location in the README with the script's relative source_dir before proposing edits.
Build a defect table: observed risk, responsible construct, required behavior, and evidence expected after a run. Use the brief to reconstruct source; do not copy an answer from a generated report.

Check six areas independently: run location, quoted paths, bounded current-log search, deterministic ordering, replacement writes, and a freshly emptied stderr destination. Trace each pipeline left to right.

The corrected source has two relative variables, an initialized run-errors file, one grouped block of report commands, and stderr redirection after the closing brace. Re-read the canonical design in the brief, write it carefully, then cat README.md and report.sh and explain every changed line.
Permission, execution, inspection, and evidence preservation are four separate actions. Predict what each can change before doing it.
Add only user execute permission, run from field-report, inspect all named report files, then create a verification directory and preserve the first summary without changing the generated original.

Use chmod u+x and direct dot-slash execution. After checking the six report paths against the brief, use mkdir for verification and copy only reports/summary.txt to verification/summary-first.txt. Explain why the copy is evidence rather than generated report source.
A repeatability test needs a before artifact, an unchanged rerun, and a comparison artifact. State exactly what an empty comparison can and cannot prove.
Run the repaired script again, then compare the saved first summary with the newly generated summary using unified diff. Save diff's stdout under verification.

Use ./report.sh for the unchanged rerun. Then use diff -u with verification/summary-first.txt first and reports/summary.txt second, redirecting comparison output to verification/repeatability.diff. Explain why success plus an empty file matters.

For each verification claim, name a path containing evidence and explain the reasoning that connects that evidence to the claim. Avoid claims broader than this clean fixture and two compared summaries.
Use six bullets: source, counts, error separation, repeatability, pipeline meaning, and permission scope. The note must explain, not merely list filenames.

Follow the six required points and wording constraints in the brief, but compose each line by pairing one claim with its evidence. Then use the final cat command named in the task and orally defend why each cited file is relevant.

tutor.goalSummary: Student independently diagnoses an inherited field-report project, repairs the executable source and documentation against immutable clean data, generates deterministic evidence with normal and error streams separated, verifies an unchanged rerun with a saved summary and empty diff, and explains how paths, pipelines, replacement, permissions, and evidence support limited correctness claims.
misconceptions: This workspace does not inherit Lesson 19 files. Primer activities are isolated, so the deliberately imperfect project and clean source are complete fresh fixtures.
A file named summary.txt is not automatically trustworthy. Provenance comes from inspecting and repairing source, rerunning it, and comparing evidence.
Relative paths resolve from the current working directory. From field-report, ../clean-data/system is correct while clean-data/system points to a nonexistent child.
find selects paths and path properties; grep selects lines inside a named file. Broadening grep to both logs changes the question being answered.
Case-insensitive error matches and an unanchored pattern admit the lowercase decoy; searching archive.log admits historical data outside current scope.
uniq removes only adjacent duplicate lines. sort must group the nonadjacent category values first and also establishes stable order.
> replaces stale generated evidence. >> is safe for summary labels only after the summary header replaced the old file during that same run.
Standard output and standard error are different streams. Diagnostic text belongs in run-errors.txt, not mixed into errors.txt or normal completion evidence.
An empty run-errors.txt means the grouped report commands emitted no diagnostics in this clean run; it does not prove failure is impossible.
chmod u+x changes permission metadata only. Mode 0744 grants owner execution without granting group or other execution and does not itself test the script.
An empty diff shows only that the two compared summary files are byte-identical. It does not prove all reports, all inputs, or all future environments are correct.
Generated reports must be regenerated from repaired source, not hand-edited. Otherwise matching text lacks reliable provenance.
Exact final files are necessary but explanation is also required: the student must connect each defect, correction, output, and evidence claim.
constraints: Keep coaching inside workspace/verification-lab, the supplied clean-data/system tree, and the field-report project defined by this activity.
Begin with observation and explanation. Ask what evidence was seen, what line could cause it, and what new evidence would test the diagnosis before suggesting a command.

Give hints in level order. Preserve student diagnosis at levels 1 and 2; at level 3 identify structure and commands for the current stage but do not provide a paste-ready complete script, README, or verification note.
Require the student to state the current directory and resolve every relative source and destination before editing, running, copying, or comparing.
Require a left-to-right explanation of every pipeline, including input scope, transformation, stdout, stderr, and final destination.
Do not accept hand-edited generated reports, matching output without source inspection, or a verification claim without named file evidence and reasoning.

Treat all clean-data paths as immutable. Permit edits only to README.md, report.sh, and VERIFICATION.md; permit script-generated reports and the two named verification evidence files under field-report.
Do not permit real /, /etc, /var, /usr, /home, absolute paths, sudo, privilege escalation, downloads, network access, or work outside verification-lab.

Do not suggest rm, mv, find -delete, find -exec, xargs, recursive grep, sed, awk, Python, eval, command substitution, process substitution, functions, arrays, background jobs, or new loops and conditions.

Keep report.sh to the canonical bounded commands and grouped stderr redirection. Require quoted variable expansions, quoted patterns, the explicitly named operations.log, sort before uniq, and replacement of generated evidence.
Use chmod u+x only. Reject chmod 777, chmod +x, or broad numeric mode replacement.

Reset after clean-source mutation, work outside the lab, broad permissions, alternate report paths, extra generated files, manual report edits, or final source text that differs from the acceptance brief.

After checks pass, require an oral defense covering isolation, path resolution, each defect and correction, find versus grep, pipeline ordering, stdout versus stderr, replacement versus append, permission scope, repeatability limits, and evidence provenance.
